transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-30 15:00 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Dr. Priya Rao (Lakeview Head of Search), Samir Patel (Platform), Denise Wu (Security), Alex Morgan (Product)

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time, we'll run through a hosted API demo focused on embeddings plus a reranker flow for clinical search, feel free to stop me at any time.

[00:00:22] Dr. Priya Rao: Sounds good, Maya. Quick context, we've got a couple of search flows — provider lookup, patient chart search, and a med knowledge base — and accuracy on the chart search is our biggest pain, lots of synonyms and shorthand in notes.

[00:00:35] Samir Patel: And from infra we care about latency; clinicians hate waiting, sub-250ms is ideal when possible, but we also have cost constraints.

[00:00:48] Maya Chen: Totally understood, that's the sweet spot of what Redwood aims for — balanced between latency and unit cost. Carlos, do you want to kick into the diagram of the flow?

[00:00:58] Carlos Ortega: Yep, quick high-level. So, two-step pattern we demo here: first, generate embeddings for your corpus and queries using our hosted embeddings endpoint; second, run a lightweight reranker on top of top-K hits to re-score and surface the best result. We'll show how you can do both with our single hosted API and the Console for tuning.

[00:01:20] Alex Morgan: When you say reranker, is that a neural model you host or is it a scoring heuristic?

[00:01:27] Carlos Ortega: Good question. Our hosted reranker is typically a small sequence scoring model — think cross-encoder style — that runs on Redwood's inference fleet. It's model-agnostic: you can pick a curated rerank model from our catalog or bring your own. For many medical cases we recommend a model fine-tuned on clinical relevance; we have a few vetted checkpoints that customers use as a starting point.

[00:01:55] Denise Wu: PHI concerns — we need to know if PHI is ever logged or retained on hosted? Does Redwood support HIPAA BAAs?

[00:02:07] Maya Chen: Short answer: yes, we support HIPAA customers under a BAA and have audit logging, KMS integrations, and data retention controls. I'll follow up with the legal security pack after the call, Denise. We'll also call out how transient KV cache works and what you can disable to minimize surface.

[00:02:28] Dr. Priya Rao: Important for us — we can't have patient identifiers persist. Also need RBAC so only the search team can access logs.

[00:02:38] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Our Console supports role-based access and you can filter logs at token-level. We'll show the Console view near the end.

[00:02:50] [00:03:10] Carlos Ortega: Alright demo time, sharing screen — I'm on the Redwood Console. First panel: model catalog. For embeddings we recommend med-embed-768 or quantized variant med-embed-384-q4 for cost-sensitive.

[00:03:30] Alex Morgan: What's the difference in quality? 768 vs 384 — is it substantial for clinical terms?

[00:03:38] Carlos Ortega: In our internal tests, med-embed-768 captures nuanced context better, particularly negation and dosages; 384 is faster and cheaper and still surprisingly robust for many lookups. For chart search we often start with 768 for top-K, then you can switch to 384 if latency becomes an issue.

[00:03:58] [00:04:20] Maya Chen: I'll pause — quick qualification: what's your monthly query volume estimate for the chart search?

[00:04:26] Samir Patel: Ballpark 1.2M queries per month across our fleet, but peak concurrent is more relevant — about 80 qps at peak clinic hours.

[00:04:36] Maya Chen: Nice, that's helpful. For 80 qps we typically recommend a combination of prefix caching and small batching windows to hit sub-250ms average.

[00:04:50] [00:05:15] Carlos Ortega: Back to the Console — here's quickstart; you can run an embeddings call in a few lines. Example call: POST /v1/embeddings with text, get vector back. Then we do approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) lookup, then rerank via POST /v1/rerank with top K candidates. I'm going to run a live example against a small sample dataset we have preloaded.

[00:05:36] [00:05:52] Carlos Ortega: (typing) Running query: "find recent notes mentioning microvascular complications and insulin regimen changes" — embedding call returns 768-dim vector in 120ms. ANN lookup returns 50 candidates in 30ms, rerank call on top 5 takes 90ms. End-to-end ~240ms in this demo environment.

[00:06:10] Dr. Priya Rao: Nice. How deterministic are rerank scores? If we adjust prompt or model version will results jump?

[00:06:20] Carlos Ortega: Rerank model versions are pinned per route; you control rollouts. We also provide eval hooks so you can run A/B on your labeled prompt sets to measure regression. Changing model can shift scores; that's why rollouts and evals are first-class in Console.

[00:06:38] [00:07:00] Alex Morgan: Can we bring custom rerank models? We have a small fine-tuned cross-encoder trained on in-house labels.

[00:07:07] Carlos Ortega: Yes, you can bring your own model artifact. For hosted we'll onboard it into our catalog after a quick compatibility test. For private deployments you can fully control it. We also support quantized variants if you want to reduce latency/cost.

[00:07:26] Denise Wu: Onboarding custom models — does that mean data (our training data) has to leave our environment? We want to avoid transfer of PHI outside our VPC.

[00:07:37] Maya Chen: If PHI is a concern, two options: use Redwood Hosted but under a BAA and with KMS and HIPAA controls enabled, or use Redwood Private deployment in your VPC/on-prem to keep training artifacts internal. We'll include both options in the security doc.

[00:07:55] [00:08:20] Samir Patel: For the hosted pilot we prefer not to run any fine-tuning that uses PHI. We can supply anonymized label sets or synthetic labels.

[00:08:30] Carlos Ortega: That works — reranker fine-tuning can be done on synthetic or de-identified examples to start. In many pilots customers use a small 1-2 week labelled set to bootstrap.

[00:08:44] [00:09:10] Maya Chen: Quick question on metrics, Priya — what do you measure for success on search? CTR? Time-to-find? Manual relevance?

[00:09:20] Dr. Priya Rao: Precision@1 and time-to-success (clinician gets correct doc) mostly. We also track false positives that could lead to wrong treatment suggestions.

[00:09:33] Maya Chen: Great, that lines up with the pilot we usually run — we propose a 30-day pilot with baseline metrics for precision@1, latency, and a small set of clinician-labeled queries.

[00:09:45] [00:10:15] Carlos Ortega: Back to the Console, I want to show rerank tuning. There is a route config where you set model_version, max_seq_len, batch_size, timeout, and fallback policies. Here's an example: for chart search we recommend max_seq_len 512, batch size 4 for rerank to keep latency <200ms in many cases. If you need lower latency we can reduce seq len or enable a quantized runner.

[00:10:38] Alex Morgan: Does batch_size 4 mean you'll accumulate requests for up to X ms to fill the batch? How does that affect p95?

[00:10:46] Carlos Ortega: Yes it's a continuous batching runtime. There's a small accumulation window (configurable) — in our autoscaling defaults it's 10-15ms. So p50 can improve without hurting p95 too much. For hard p95 SLOs you can set max_wait_ms to 0 to disable batching and rely on single-request execution.

[00:11:08] [00:11:40] Denise Wu: Audit logs: need to show who accessed what, and also redaction support in logs for PHI fields. Is that native?

[00:11:50] Maya Chen: We export structured audit logs to your S3 or GCS and you can configure redaction rules. Also integrates with SIEM. We'll include a sample redaction policy in the security pack.

[00:12:05] Dr. Priya Rao: Can you talk about memory of KV cache and if that persists across requests? Concerned about inadvertent leakage of PHI in cache.

[00:12:18] Carlos Ortega: KV cache in our runtime is ephemeral for generation; for embeddings/rerank flows we don't persist user inputs beyond what you opt-in for analytics or to improve caching. For extra safety you can disable caching entirely for specific routes.

[00:12:36] [00:13:05] Maya Chen: Switching to the Optimize tab — Redwood Optimize will give batching and quantization suggestions based on observed sequence length distributions. You can simulate cost impact in the Console. Here's a sample report: switching from 768 to 384 reduced token-cost by ~40% in a mixed workload with a small 5% hit to precision@1 in one of our internal evals for clinical notes.

[00:13:31] Samir Patel: How accurate are those simulations vs production? We worry about underestimating p95 latency.

[00:13:38] Carlos Ortega: Simulations use your supplied sample distribution and our runtime models. They're estimates; we always recommend running a short production canary to validate. We also provide tracing so you can root cause slow path (e.g., long seqs causing kernel fallback).

[00:13:59] [00:14:30] Alex Morgan: Any specific quantization formats you recommend? We are GPU-based in our infra.

[00:14:37] Carlos Ortega: For hosted you can choose q4_0 or q8_0 variants; q4_0 often gives the best speed/cost balance. On GPUs we do kernel selection automatically, but we can also surface the compiled profile if you want to review.

[00:14:53] Dr. Priya Rao: In practice, do you see hallucinations in reranker output for clinical strings? Risk is wrong instructions downstream.

[00:15:03] Carlos Ortega: Rerankers typically don't hallucinate like a generator, since they score candidate passages. The main risk is model bias — e.g., scoring an irrelevant note high if training labels were noisy. That's why label quality and eval sets are key.

[00:15:21] [00:15:45] Maya Chen: Let's look at a short live failure mode — I will run a query purposely ambiguous: "insulin adjustment" and show top-K where a note referencing historical insulin change appears above a more recent change. You can see how reranker rescoring based on recency and context can demote old entries.

[00:16:08] Carlos Ortega: (shows logs) Here's trace for the rerank call — timestamps and token counts. You can see model_version pinned and the fallback to a smaller quantized runner for large seqs.

[00:16:25] Denise Wu: Do traces include the full patient note content? We need to avoid logs containing PHI unless redaction is on.

[00:16:33] Maya Chen: By default traces have token-level stats, not full text; content logging is opt-in and we can disable it for the pilot.

[00:16:46] [00:17:10] Alex Morgan: If we do a pilot, what's the minimal data you need to show improvement? 200 labeled queries? 500?

[00:17:18] Carlos Ortega: For measurable lift on precision@1, we typically want 200–500 labeled positives across intents. For significance you'd aim for 1k+. For an initial pilot 200 curated queries plus clinician labels is a reasonable start.

[00:17:36] Dr. Priya Rao: We can do 250 queries per intent, 3 intents. We'll anonymize PHI.

[00:17:45] [00:18:12] Maya Chen: Great — next steps then: we'll send security docs and pilot pricing. Carlos will send a quickstart notebook that shows how to call embeddings + ANN + rerank and a sample evaluation harness to compute precision@k.

[00:18:28] Carlos Ortega: I'll share a colab and a small Docker image to reproduce the rerank loop. Link: https://redwood.example.com/quickstarts/lakeview-demo (placeholder).

[00:18:44] Samir Patel: For legal, Denise will need the BAA template.

[00:18:50] Denise Wu: Yes, also want to know about data residency — can hosted operate in our preferred region? We need US-only.

[00:18:57] Maya Chen: Yes, our hosted API has region controls and we can pin your workload to US regions. We'll include region routing details in the security pack.

[00:19:10] [00:19:40] Carlos Ortega: Quick dev note: ANN service can be colocated in your VPC for hybrid setups; that lowers egress and can speed up retrieval. We can discuss if you want a hybrid pilot.

[00:19:58] Alex Morgan: Hybrid sounds interesting — what's the complexity?

[00:20:03] Carlos Ortega: It requires a small connectivity setup and a Docker image we run in your VPC; Redwood still manages the model runtime unless you opt for Private. It's a middle ground sometimes called "private compute".

[00:20:20] [00:20:52] Dr. Priya Rao: Pricing — any idea of pilot costs?

[00:20:58] Maya Chen: For pilots we generally offer a capped pilot plan that includes up to X tokens/embeddings and rerank calls. I'll put numbers in the follow-up but expect a heavily discounted trial to validate lift.

[00:21:15] Samir Patel: On instrumentation — can we push traces to our OpenTelemetry stack?

[00:21:23] Carlos Ortega: Yes, we support OTLP export for traces and metrics.

[00:21:35] [00:21:55] Maya Chen: Quick demo of the Console's Eval page — you can upload labeled pairs and run automatic comparisons across model versions. It produces precision@k, MRR, and a small error breakdown.

[00:22:12] Alex Morgan: Can we automate alerts if precision drops post-rollout?

[00:22:18] Carlos Ortega: Yes, Redwood Optimize integrates with monitoring to alert on regression thresholds.

[00:22:30] [00:23:00] Denise Wu: SSO & provisioning — we need SAML and SCIM to provision developer accounts.

[00:23:08] Maya Chen: We support SAML SSO and SCIM user provisioning, and can enforce MFA. We'll include our SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint docs.

[00:23:25] Dr. Priya Rao: Time check — couple more minutes?

[00:23:29] Maya Chen: Sure, quick Q&A.

[00:23:35] Alex Morgan: Are there limits on model size in hosted? Could we bring a larger cross-encoder?

[00:23:42] Carlos Ortega: Hosted supports a wide variety; very large models are fine but may increase cost and slightly higher latency. For rerank we usually keep it compact (<1.5B) to meet sub-250ms. If you need >1.5B we can still run it but recommend Dedicated or Private.

[00:24:00] [00:24:30] Samir Patel: Will you allow us to run a baseline shadow test before going live? Send traffic but not surfaced to clinicians?

[00:24:38] Maya Chen: Absolutely — that's a standard step. Shadow mode and canary traffic splitting are supported.

[00:24:50] Dr. Priya Rao: Any stories from other health customers?

[00:24:56] Carlos Ortega: Without naming specifics, we helped a hospital system reduce time-to-find by 35% using a similar rerank + region-pin approach. We can share an anonymized case study.

[00:25:10] [00:25:40] Maya Chen: We're about halfway through timewise — do you want us to run one more live sample or wrap and move to next steps?

[00:25:48] Dr. Priya Rao: Wrap is fine, the demo covered what we needed.

[00:25:54] Maya Chen: Great. Quick recap — Redwood will: 1) send security artifacts including HIPAA/BAA info and region controls, 2) Carlos to share quickstart notebook + rerank Docker, 3) Maya to follow up with pilot pricing and schedule kickoff week of 12/7. Customer will: provide 3 intents and 200 anonymized queries each, and Samir to send traffic profile.

[00:26:21] Denise Wu: We'll review BAA and decide whether to do hosted pilot or hybrid.

[00:26:28] Alex Morgan: Thanks — appreciate the clear path.

[00:26:33] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone, we'll send notes and links right after.

[00:26:38] [00:56:00] TRANSCRIPT NOTES: End of recorded portion. There are short pauses and some cross-talk in Q&A; some product names were mis-transcribed by auto speech (e.g., 'med-embed-768' appeared as 'med embed seven six eight' in some points). Links mentioned: https://redwood.example.com/quickstarts/lakeview-demo, security pack placeholder at https://redwood.example.com/security/lakeview-hipaa.
